decided_by: anomalica/master, applying Mark's ruling of 2026-09-02; put to Mark with a 30-minute veto window before deploy
rule: A page is not written for a person who is only mentioned. The page gate's person tier requires the person to be the subject of at least 3 claims (assimilator page_gate, MIN_SUBJECT_CLAIMS=3). Pages built before that rule existed and failing it today are retired if they are mention-stubs, kept if they are substantial articles - the gate decides what gets made, not what gets unmade, and a substantial page is rewritten as subject claims arrive rather than removed.
method: Read-only sweep over every live page under content/pages/people, each resolved to its graph node through its brief; subject counts from the assimilator's own page_gate._subject_counts called against knowledge.db; a node absent from that count is the subject of zero claims. Word count is body prose without citation markers; inbound links are exact markdown links from any page in any language.

not_assessable: chris (no brief; retired separately as an unidentifiable first-name figure)
uap-gerb (no brief; moved to its survivor's slug)

retired.note: bare first name, same footing as chris

kept.why: substantial, well-cited; the corpus discusses him constantly; rewritten as subject claims arrive

effects: Nineteen inbound links across the ten render as plain text after the build, by design (the site strips a link whose target does not exist). No redirects: these are people, not duplicates, and a wrong destination is worse than an honest 404. Each URL carries a gone: true entry with a note in site/data/redirects.yaml.
how_to_reverse_one: git checkout <retirement commit>^ -- content/pages/people/<slug>.en.md ; remove the URL's entry from site/data/redirects.yaml ; push both ; site deploys. Any reviewer may do this for any single page without touching the others.
